facts.title: A Tiger's Roar Can Travel Two Miles xFunFacts
facts.summary: [xFunFacts] A tiger's roar can travel up to two miles, helping these solitary predators communicate across vast territories.

facts.title: A Turkey's Head Changes Color xFunFacts
facts.summary: [xFunFacts] A turkey's head changes color with mood, excitement, and breeding displays through changes in blood flow.

facts.title: A Woodpecker Can Peck 20 Times per Second xFunFacts
facts.summary: [xFunFacts] A woodpecker can peck up to 20 times per second thanks to specialized skull structures that absorb repeated impacts.

facts.title: A Woodpecker's Tongue Wraps Around Its Brain xFunFacts
facts.summary: [xFunFacts] A woodpecker's tongue wraps around its skull, helping it feed efficiently and withstand repeated pecking impacts.
facts.alt: Woodpecker showing tongue wrapped around its skull

facts.title: Adult Cats Can Be Lactose Intolerant xFunFacts
facts.summary: [xFunFacts] Many adult cats become lactose intolerant, so ordinary cow's milk can lead to digestive discomfort.

facts.title: Adult Dogs Have Exactly 42 Teeth xFunFacts
facts.summary: [xFunFacts] An adult dog normally has 42 permanent teeth. They include incisors, canines, premolars, and molars used for different functions.

facts.title: Adult Polar Bears Can Weigh Over 700 Kilograms xFunFacts
facts.summary: [xFunFacts] Adult polar bears can weigh more than 700 kilograms, making them among the heaviest land predators alive today.

facts.title: African Elephants Have Bigger Ears xFunFacts
facts.summary: [xFunFacts] African elephants have much larger ears than Asian elephants, helping them stay cool in hot climates.

facts.title: African Elephants Have Four Functional Molars xFunFacts
facts.summary: [xFunFacts] African elephants have four working molars at a time and replace them with six sets throughout their lives.

facts.title: African Grey Parrots Can Learn Hundreds of Words xFunFacts
facts.summary: [xFunFacts] African grey parrots can learn hundreds of words and are among the world's most intelligent bird species.
facts.alt: African grey parrot perched on a branch

facts.title: African Rock Pythons Can Survive Long Periods Without Food xFunFacts
facts.summary: [xFunFacts] African rock pythons can survive for months or even years without food by dramatically slowing their metabolism after large meals.
facts.alt: African rock python resting after feeding

facts.title: All Clownfish Are Born Male xFunFacts
facts.summary: [xFunFacts] Every clownfish begins life as a male, and the largest male can become female if the dominant female disappears.
facts.alt: Clownfish changing from male to female

facts.title: All Insects Have Six Legs xFunFacts
facts.summary: [xFunFacts] Every insect has six legs, one of the defining characteristics that separates insects from other arthropods.
facts.alt: Close-up of an insect with six legs

facts.title: All Owls Lay White Eggs xFunFacts
facts.summary: [xFunFacts] All owls lay white eggs, a characteristic shared across owl species regardless of their size or habitat.

facts.title: All Snakes Are Carnivores xFunFacts
facts.summary: [xFunFacts] All snakes are carnivores, feeding exclusively on animals ranging from insects and fish to birds and mammals.

facts.title: Alligators and Crocodiles Share One Wild Habitat xFunFacts
facts.summary: [xFunFacts] Florida's Everglades is the world's only natural habitat where wild alligators and crocodiles live side by side.
facts.alt: Alligator and crocodile in the Everglades

facts.title: American White Pelicans Can Hold Three Gallons of Water xFunFacts
facts.summary: [xFunFacts] The American white pelican's enormous throat pouch can hold up to three gallons of water while catching fish.

facts.title: An African Elephant's Skeleton Is About 15% of Its Body Weight xFunFacts
facts.summary: [xFunFacts] An African elephant's skeleton makes up about 15% of its body weight, providing strength for the world's largest land animal.

facts.title: An Alaskan Town Once Had a Cat Mayor xFunFacts
facts.summary: [xFunFacts] An Alaska town once became famous for having a cat named Stubbs serve as its beloved honorary mayor for many years.

facts.title: An Elephant Produces About 22 Kilograms of Dung Each Day xFunFacts
facts.summary: [xFunFacts] An elephant produces about 22 kilograms of dung daily, helping spread seeds and enrich ecosystems across its habitat.
facts.alt: Elephant beside a pile of dung

facts.title: An Elephant's Trunk Can Hold Several Liters of Water xFunFacts
facts.summary: [xFunFacts] An elephant's trunk can hold several liters of water before spraying it into the mouth or over the body.
facts.alt: Elephant spraying water with its trunk

facts.title: An Elephant's Trunk Has Over 40,000 Muscles xFunFacts
facts.summary: [xFunFacts] An elephant's trunk contains over 40,000 muscles, allowing incredible strength, precision, and flexibility.

facts.title: An Immortal Jellyfish Can Restart Its Life Cycle xFunFacts
facts.summary: [xFunFacts] The immortal jellyfish can reset its life cycle, making it one of nature's most fascinating animals.

facts.title: An Octopus Has Rectangular Pupils xFunFacts
facts.summary: [xFunFacts] An octopus has rectangular pupils that help regulate incoming light and improve underwater vision.

facts.title: An Ostrich Can Outrun a Horse xFunFacts
facts.summary: [xFunFacts] An ostrich can outrun a horse over long distances thanks to its powerful legs, efficient stride, and remarkable endurance.

facts.title: An Ostrich Lives 40 to 45 Years xFunFacts
facts.summary: [xFunFacts] Ostriches typically live 40 to 45 years, making them one of the longest-lived bird species in the world.

facts.title: An Ostrich's Eye Is Bigger Than Its Brain xFunFacts
facts.summary: [xFunFacts] An ostrich's eye is larger than its brain, giving the world's biggest bird exceptional vision for spotting predators.

facts.title: An Ostrich's Small Intestine Can Reach 14 Meters xFunFacts
facts.summary: [xFunFacts] An adult ostrich's small intestine can reach about 14 meters, helping digest large amounts of plant-based food efficiently.

facts.title: An Oyster Takes About Five Years to Grow a Pearl xFunFacts
facts.summary: [xFunFacts] A cultured oyster typically needs about five years to produce a medium-sized pearl through layers of natural nacre.

facts.title: Ant Queens Can Live for 30 Years xFunFacts
facts.summary: [xFunFacts] While worker ants often live only a short time, a queen can survive for decades and rule the same colony for years.

facts.title: Antarctica Has No Native Reptiles or Snakes xFunFacts
facts.summary: [xFunFacts] Antarctica is the only continent without native reptiles or snakes because its extreme climate is too cold for them to survive.
facts.alt: Antarctica without native reptiles or snakes

facts.title: Anteaters Have No Teeth xFunFacts
facts.summary: [xFunFacts] Anteaters have no teeth and rely on long sticky tongues to catch thousands of insects each day.

facts.title: Ants Breathe Without Lungs xFunFacts
facts.summary: [xFunFacts] Ants breathe through tiny spiracles and air tubes instead of using lungs like mammals do.

facts.title: Ants Can Carry 50 Times Their Own Weight xFunFacts
facts.summary: [xFunFacts] Ants can carry objects up to 50 times their own weight thanks to their powerful muscles and small size.

facts.title: Ants Don't Like Baby Powder xFunFacts
facts.summary: [xFunFacts] Baby powder can disrupt the scent trails ants rely on for navigation, making it a simple but temporary way to discourage them.

facts.title: Ants Smell With Their Antennae, Not Noses xFunFacts
facts.summary: [xFunFacts] Ants communicate through chemical signals detected with their antennae, not noses. This sophisticated system allows colonies to work together with remarkable efficiency.
facts.alt: Ants touching antennae to detect chemical pheromone signals

facts.title: Ants Stretch After Resting xFunFacts
facts.summary: [xFunFacts] Researchers have observed ants stretching after resting, showing that even tiny insects display recovery behaviors.

facts.title: Armadillos Can Walk Underwater xFunFacts
facts.summary: [xFunFacts] Armadillos can walk underwater by holding their breath and crossing streambeds instead of swimming.
facts.alt: Armadillo walking underwater across a stream

facts.title: Armadillos Have Extremely Tough Armor xFunFacts
facts.summary: [xFunFacts] Armadillos have remarkably tough protective armor, but the idea that they are bulletproof is only a myth.

facts.title: Armadillos Usually Give Birth to Four Identical Babies xFunFacts
facts.summary: [xFunFacts] Nine-banded armadillos usually give birth to four genetically identical babies that are always the same sex.
facts.alt: Nine-banded armadillo with four baby armadillos

facts.title: August 17 Is Black Cat Appreciation Day xFunFacts
facts.summary: [xFunFacts] August 17 is celebrated as Black Cat Appreciation Day. The annual event encourages people to appreciate black cats and challenge old superstitions.

facts.title: Australia Has More Camels Than Egypt xFunFacts
facts.summary: [xFunFacts] Australia has more wild camels than Egypt, with descendants of nineteenth-century transport animals roaming the Outback.
facts.alt: Wild camels in the Australian outback

facts.title: Australia Has More Kangaroos Than People xFunFacts
facts.summary: [xFunFacts] Australia often has more kangaroos than people, with wildlife numbers changing widely according to rainfall, drought, and food supply.

facts.title: Axolotls Also Breathe Through Their Skin xFunFacts
facts.summary: [xFunFacts] Axolotls breathe through both their gills and skin, with simple lungs providing additional oxygen when needed.

facts.title: Axolotls Can Live for 15 Years xFunFacts
facts.summary: [xFunFacts] With proper care, axolotls can live up to 15 years, far longer than many other amphibians.

facts.title: Axolotls Can Reach One Foot Long xFunFacts
facts.summary: [xFunFacts] Axolotls can grow up to 12 inches long, though most adults are slightly smaller in captivity.

facts.title: Axolotls Can Regrow Almost Any Body Part xFunFacts
facts.summary: [xFunFacts] Axolotls can regenerate limbs, organs, and even parts of the brain, making them unique in the animal kingdom.

facts.title: Axolotls Have External Gills xFunFacts
facts.summary: [xFunFacts] Axolotls have feathery external gills that absorb oxygen and give them their distinctive appearance.

facts.title: Axolotls Never Truly Grow Up xFunFacts
facts.summary: [xFunFacts] Axolotls remain in their larval stage for life while still reaching adulthood and reproducing successfully.

facts.title: Baby Blue Whales Can Gain 200 Pounds a Day xFunFacts
facts.summary: [xFunFacts] Baby blue whales can gain around 200 pounds each day while feeding on their mother's rich, high-fat milk.
facts.alt: Blue whale calf swimming with its mother

facts.title: 20,000 Bees Followed a Car for Two Days xFunFacts
facts.summary: [xFunFacts] Around 20,000 bees followed a car for two days after their queen became trapped inside. The remarkable swarm stayed together until rescuers safely reunited the colony.
facts.alt: Swarm of bees following a car

facts.title: A Baby Giraffe Is About 1.8 Meters Tall at Birth xFunFacts
facts.summary: [xFunFacts] A newborn giraffe stands about 1.8 meters tall and can usually stand and walk within hours of birth.

facts.title: A Beehive Can Hold 60,000 Bees xFunFacts
facts.summary: [xFunFacts] A healthy beehive can contain up to 60,000 bees working together in a highly organized colony.

facts.title: A Beehive Stays as Warm as the Human Body xFunFacts
facts.summary: [xFunFacts] A healthy beehive stays close to human body temperature throughout the year. Bees regulate the warmth by vibrating their flight muscles and fanning their wings.

facts.title: A Blue Whale Can Weigh as Much as 30 Elephants xFunFacts
facts.summary: [xFunFacts] A blue whale can weigh as much as 30 elephants, making it the largest animal known to have ever lived on Earth.
facts.alt: Blue whale beside elephants for size comparison

facts.title: A Blue Whale's Heartbeat Can Be Heard Miles Away xFunFacts
facts.summary: [xFunFacts] A blue whale's enormous heartbeat can sometimes be detected from more than two miles away underwater.

facts.title: A Blue Whale's Tongue Can Weigh as Much as an Elephant xFunFacts
facts.summary: [xFunFacts] A blue whale's tongue can weigh as much as an adult elephant, reflecting the enormous scale of the world's largest animal.

facts.title: A Bumblebee Flaps Its Wings 160 Times per Second xFunFacts
facts.summary: [xFunFacts] A bumblebee flaps its wings about 160 times per second, allowing precise hovering and efficient flower pollination.

facts.title: A Chameleon's Tongue Can Be Twice Its Body Length xFunFacts
facts.summary: [xFunFacts] Some chameleons can extend their tongues to twice their body length when catching insects with remarkable speed.
facts.alt: Chameleon catching an insect with its tongue

facts.title: A Chicken Once Flew for 13 Seconds xFunFacts
facts.summary: [xFunFacts] A chicken's longest recorded flight lasted about 13 seconds, showing how these birds use short bursts of flight to escape danger.
facts.alt: Chicken flapping its wings in midair

facts.title: A Chicken Survived 18 Months Without Its Head xFunFacts
facts.summary: [xFunFacts] Mike the Headless Chicken survived for 18 months after losing most of his head in a farming accident.

facts.title: A Child Could Swim Through a Blue Whale Artery xFunFacts
facts.summary: [xFunFacts] A blue whale's largest arteries are so enormous that a child could theoretically fit inside one. Its massive anatomy reflects the size of Earth's largest animal.
facts.alt: Blue whale heart and giant artery comparison

facts.title: A Crocodile's Bite Is Strong but Its Jaw Opens Weakly xFunFacts
facts.summary: [xFunFacts] Saltwater crocodiles have the strongest recorded bite force of any living animal. Surprisingly, the muscles used to open their jaws are relatively weak.

facts.title: A Dragonfly Can Fly at 40 km/h xFunFacts
facts.summary: [xFunFacts] Dragonflies can fly at speeds of around 40 km/h while performing remarkable aerial maneuvers to catch prey.

facts.title: A Flamingo's "Backwards Knee" Is Actually Its Ankle xFunFacts
facts.summary: [xFunFacts] What appears to be a flamingo's backward knee is actually its ankle, while the true knee is hidden higher up.

facts.title: A Flea Can Jump 100 Times Its Body Length xFunFacts
facts.summary: [xFunFacts] Fleas can jump up to 100 times their body length using a spring-like protein called resilin.

facts.title: A Flea Can Jump About 350 Times Its Body Length xFunFacts
facts.summary: [xFunFacts] A flea can jump about 350 times its body length, making it one of the most powerful jumpers relative to size.

facts.title: A Fly Reacts in Just 30 Milliseconds xFunFacts
facts.summary: [xFunFacts] A fly reacts in about 30 milliseconds, giving it incredibly fast reflexes that help it escape predators and swatting hands.
facts.alt: Fly taking off from a surface

facts.title: A Giant Pacific Octopus Can Fit Through a Hole the Size of Its Beak xFunFacts
facts.summary: [xFunFacts] A giant Pacific octopus can squeeze through any opening larger than its beak, despite its enormous overall size.
facts.alt: Giant Pacific octopus squeezing through a small hole

facts.title: A Giraffe Can Clean Its Ears with Its Tongue xFunFacts
facts.summary: [xFunFacts] A giraffe's tongue can reach its own ears, helping it clean them while also feeding on thorny trees.
facts.alt: Giraffe touching its ear with its tongue

facts.title: A Giraffe's Tongue Can Reach 20 Inches xFunFacts
facts.summary: [xFunFacts] A giraffe's tongue can grow to around 20 inches long, helping it feed among thorny branches and clean its face.

facts.title: A Grizzly Bear Can Crush a Bowling Ball with Its Bite xFunFacts
facts.summary: [xFunFacts] A grizzly bear's bite can exceed 1,000 PSI, giving it enough force to crush bones and even a bowling ball.

facts.title: A Group of Hummingbirds Has Many Beautiful Names xFunFacts
facts.summary: [xFunFacts] A group of hummingbirds may be called a hover, glittering, bouquet, tune, or shimmer, inspired by their dazzling appearance.

facts.title: A Group of Lemurs Is Called a Conspiracy xFunFacts
facts.summary: [xFunFacts] A group of lemurs isn't called a troop or a pack. The official collective noun is the surprisingly fitting "conspiracy."

facts.title: A Group of Parrots Is Called a Pandemonium xFunFacts
facts.summary: [xFunFacts] A group of parrots is collectively known as a pandemonium. The unusual name reflects the birds' loud and energetic behavior.

facts.title: A Group of Rhinos Is Called a Crash xFunFacts
facts.summary: [xFunFacts] A group of rhinos is officially called a "crash," making it one of the most memorable collective nouns in the English language.

facts.title: A Hamster's Teeth Never Stop Growing xFunFacts
facts.summary: [xFunFacts] A hamster's teeth grow continuously throughout its life, requiring constant chewing to keep them trimmed.
facts.alt: Hamster chewing to wear down teeth

facts.title: A Hen Can Lay Around 250 Eggs a Year xFunFacts
facts.summary: [xFunFacts] A healthy laying hen can produce around 250 eggs each year, depending on breed, nutrition, and living conditions.

facts.title: A Hibernating Bear Can Lose 25% of Its Body Weight xFunFacts
facts.summary: [xFunFacts] During hibernation, a bear can lose up to 25% of its body weight while surviving almost entirely on stored fat.

facts.title: A Hippo Can Open Its Mouth Wide Enough to Fit a Child xFunFacts
facts.summary: [xFunFacts] A hippopotamus can open its mouth wide enough to fit a child, supported by one of the strongest bites among land mammals.

facts.title: A Horse Produces More Than One Horsepower xFunFacts
facts.summary: [xFunFacts] A healthy horse can briefly generate around 24 horsepower, far exceeding the unit of measurement named after it.

facts.title: A Hummingbird's Heart Can Beat Over 1,000 Times a Minute xFunFacts
facts.summary: [xFunFacts] A hummingbird's heart can beat more than 1,000 times per minute during active flight to support its rapid metabolism.

facts.title: A Lion’s Roar Can Be Heard 5 Miles Away xFunFacts
facts.summary: [xFunFacts] A lion's roar can travel up to five miles under the right conditions. Powerful vocal cords help lions communicate across vast territories.
facts.alt: Roaring lion in the African savanna

facts.title: A Lion's Tongue Feels Like Sandpaper xFunFacts
facts.summary: [xFunFacts] A lion's rough tongue feels like sandpaper because it is covered with tiny spines that help strip meat from prey.

facts.title: A Male Baboon Can Kill a Leopard xFunFacts
facts.summary: [xFunFacts] Large male baboons can seriously injure or even kill leopards when defending themselves or protecting their troop.

facts.title: A Male Lion's Mane Is More Than Decoration xFunFacts
facts.summary: [xFunFacts] A male lion's mane helps shield its neck during fights while also signaling strength, health, and maturity.
facts.alt: Male lion with a full mane

facts.title: A Mosquito Lives About Two Weeks xFunFacts
facts.summary: [xFunFacts] Many mosquitoes live for about two weeks, though lifespan varies by species, sex, climate, and environmental conditions.

facts.title: A Newborn Kangaroo Is Only About One Inch Long xFunFacts
facts.summary: [xFunFacts] A newborn kangaroo is only about one inch long at birth before completing its journey to the mother's pouch for continued development.

facts.title: A Pigeon's Bones Weigh Less Than Its Feathers xFunFacts
facts.summary: [xFunFacts] A pigeon's lightweight skeleton weighs less than its feathers, helping make flight more efficient.

facts.title: A Platypus Can Eat Its Own Weight in Worms xFunFacts
facts.summary: [xFunFacts] A platypus can eat food equal to its own body weight in a day to support its active lifestyle and rapid metabolism.

facts.title: A Poison Dart Frog Can Kill Over 2,200 People xFunFacts
facts.summary: [xFunFacts] The most poisonous poison dart frogs carry enough toxin to kill over 2,200 people, making them among Earth's most toxic animals.
facts.alt: Poison dart frog on a rainforest leaf

facts.title: A Porcupine Can Have Around 30,000 Quills xFunFacts
facts.summary: [xFunFacts] A porcupine can have around 30,000 quills that provide effective protection against predators.

facts.title: A Queen Bee Can Lay 3,000 Eggs in One Day xFunFacts
facts.summary: [xFunFacts] A healthy queen bee can lay up to 3,000 eggs in one day, keeping a thriving hive active and growing.

facts.title: A Severed Snake Head Can Still Bite xFunFacts
facts.summary: [xFunFacts] A severed snake head can still bite and inject venom for a short time. Residual nerve activity keeps the reflex functioning after death.

facts.title: A Shrimp's Heart Is Located in Its Head xFunFacts
facts.summary: [xFunFacts] A shrimp's heart is located inside its head region, one of the many unusual features of crustacean anatomy.

facts.title: A Shrimp's Organs Float in Its Blood xFunFacts
facts.summary: [xFunFacts] Shrimp have an open circulatory system where many internal organs are surrounded directly by circulating hemolymph.

facts.title: A Sloth's Fur Grows Upward xFunFacts
facts.summary: [xFunFacts] A sloth's fur grows upward to help rainwater drain away while it hangs upside down.
facts.alt: Sloth hanging upside down in a tree

facts.title: A Snail Needs About 220 Hours to Crawl One Mile xFunFacts
facts.summary: [xFunFacts] A snail would need roughly 220 hours of nonstop movement to crawl a single mile.

facts.title: A Snail Stayed Glued in a Museum for Four Years - While Alive xFunFacts
facts.summary: [xFunFacts] A museum snail was accidentally glued to a display card and remained there for four years before anyone realized it was still alive.

facts.title: A Squid Has 10 Appendages xFunFacts
facts.summary: [xFunFacts] Squid have eight arms and two feeding tentacles, giving them 10 appendages perfectly adapted for hunting in the ocean.
facts.alt: Squid with labeled arms and tentacles

facts.title: Baby Elephants Are Called Calves xFunFacts
facts.summary: [xFunFacts] Baby elephants are called calves and receive care and protection from the entire family herd.

facts.title: Baby Elephants Suck Their Trunks for Comfort xFunFacts
facts.summary: [xFunFacts] Baby elephants sometimes suck their trunks for comfort, much like young children suck their thumbs.

facts.title: Baby Flamingos Aren't Born Pink xFunFacts
facts.summary: [xFunFacts] Baby flamingos hatch with gray feathers and gradually turn pink after eating foods rich in natural pigments.
facts.alt: Gray baby flamingo beside pink adult flamingo

facts.title: Baby Hedgehogs Grow Their Spines Within 24 Hours xFunFacts
facts.summary: [xFunFacts] Baby hedgehogs begin growing their protective spines within 24 hours, giving them an early defense against predators.

facts.title: Baby Horses Can Run Within Hours xFunFacts
facts.summary: [xFunFacts] Baby horses can stand, walk, and even run within just a few hours of birth. Their rapid development helps them survive in the wild.

facts.title: Baby Pandas Are Pink and Baby Flamingos Are White xFunFacts
facts.summary: [xFunFacts] Baby pandas are born pink, while flamingos hatch white before their diet gradually turns them pink.

facts.title: Baby Pandas Are Smaller Than a Mouse at Birth xFunFacts
facts.summary: [xFunFacts] A newborn giant panda is so unbelievably tiny that it starts life smaller than many mice.
facts.alt: Newborn giant panda smaller than a mouse

facts.title: Baby Polar Bears Can't See or Hear at Birth xFunFacts
facts.summary: [xFunFacts] Baby polar bears are born blind and deaf, depending entirely on their mother during the first weeks of life.

facts.title: Baby Rabbits Are Called a Litter xFunFacts
facts.summary: [xFunFacts] A group of baby rabbits is called a litter, while each baby is known as a kit or kitten. These terms are commonly used by breeders and veterinarians.

facts.title: Baby Rattlesnakes Are Born in Late Summer xFunFacts
facts.summary: [xFunFacts] Baby rattlesnakes are typically born in late summer and are fully equipped with venom and fangs from birth.

facts.title: Barn Owls Have Heart-Shaped Faces xFunFacts
facts.summary: [xFunFacts] Barn owls are known for their heart-shaped faces, which help funnel sound for incredibly accurate hunting.

facts.title: Basenjis Are Known as the Barkless Dog xFunFacts
facts.summary: [xFunFacts] Basenjis are known as the barkless dog because they produce a unique yodel-like sound instead of barking.

facts.title: Bats Are Not Blind xFunFacts
facts.summary: [xFunFacts] Bats are not blind. Most species have good eyesight and combine vision with echolocation to navigate and hunt.

facts.title: Bats Are the Only Mammals That Can Truly Fly xFunFacts
facts.summary: [xFunFacts] Bats are the only mammals capable of sustained powered flight, using specialized wings unlike any other mammal.

facts.title: Bats Cannot Walk Like Most Mammals xFunFacts
facts.summary: [xFunFacts] Bats cannot walk like most mammals because their legs evolved primarily for hanging and powered flight.
facts.alt: Bat hanging upside down instead of walking

facts.title: Bats Have Excellent Hearing xFunFacts
facts.summary: [xFunFacts] Bats have exceptional hearing that supports echolocation, allowing precise navigation and hunting in darkness.

facts.title: Bear Cubs Are Tiny at Birth xFunFacts
facts.summary: [xFunFacts] Bear cubs are born during hibernation weighing less than one pound and depend entirely on their mother for survival.

facts.title: Bears Can Use Simple Tools xFunFacts
facts.summary: [xFunFacts] Some bears have been observed using sticks as simple tools, showing impressive problem-solving abilities.

facts.title: Bears Have an Extraordinary Sense of Smell xFunFacts
facts.summary: [xFunFacts] Bears have an extraordinary sense of smell that helps them locate food, mates, and danger from great distances.

facts.title: Bees and Houseflies Beat Their Wings 200 Times a Second xFunFacts
facts.summary: [xFunFacts] Bees and houseflies beat their wings about 200 times each second, creating the familiar buzzing sound of flight.

facts.title: Bees Are Essential Pollinators xFunFacts
facts.summary: [xFunFacts] Bees pollinate countless crops and wild plants, making them essential for healthy ecosystems and global food production.

facts.title: Bees Can Recognize Human Faces xFunFacts
facts.summary: [xFunFacts] Research shows bees can recognize human faces by learning and remembering visual patterns.

facts.title: Bees Can See Ultraviolet Light xFunFacts
facts.summary: [xFunFacts] Bees can see ultraviolet light, allowing them to spot hidden flower patterns that guide them to nectar.

facts.title: Bees Have a Honey Stomach xFunFacts
facts.summary: [xFunFacts] Bees store nectar in a specialized honey stomach before carrying it back to the hive to make honey.

facts.title: Bees Have Five Eyes xFunFacts
facts.summary: [xFunFacts] Bees have five eyes that help them detect movement, light, and flowers rich in nectar.

facts.title: Bees Live on Every Continent Except Antarctica xFunFacts
facts.summary: [xFunFacts] Bees naturally inhabit every continent except Antarctica, where the climate cannot support their survival.
facts.alt: Honeybee collecting nectar from a flower

facts.title: Bees Really Do Have Knees xFunFacts
facts.summary: [xFunFacts] Bees really do have knees, making one of the English language's most famous expressions surprisingly accurate.

facts.title: Birds Need Gravity to Swallow xFunFacts
facts.summary: [xFunFacts] Many birds rely on gravity to help swallow food, unlike humans who use stronger swallowing muscles.
facts.alt: Bird swallowing food with its head raised

facts.title: Birds Often Ride on Capybaras xFunFacts
facts.summary: [xFunFacts] Birds often perch on capybaras to eat insects in their fur, creating a mutually beneficial partnership.

facts.title: Black Widow Spiders Have an Hourglass Mark xFunFacts
facts.summary: [xFunFacts] Female black widow spiders are recognized by the distinctive red hourglass marking on the underside of their abdomen.

facts.title: Blue Lobsters Are Extremely Rare xFunFacts
facts.summary: [xFunFacts] Blue lobsters are incredibly rare, appearing in about one out of every two million because of a genetic mutation.

facts.title: Blue Whale Blood Vessels Are Huge xFunFacts
facts.summary: [xFunFacts] Blue whale arteries are so enormous that a person could theoretically swim through one of the largest blood vessels.
facts.alt: Blue whale artery compared with a human figure

facts.title: Blue Whales Are the Largest Animals Ever xFunFacts
facts.summary: [xFunFacts] Blue whales are the largest animals ever known, growing longer and heavier than any dinosaur that has ever been discovered.

facts.title: Blue Whales Can Go Months Without Eating xFunFacts
facts.summary: [xFunFacts] Blue whales can survive for months without eating by relying on thick layers of stored body fat during migration.
facts.alt: Blue whale swimming in the deep ocean

facts.title: Blue-Eyed Cats Are More Likely to Be Deaf xFunFacts
facts.summary: [xFunFacts] Blue eyes may look striking on a cat, but in white cats they also come with a much higher chance of hearing loss.

facts.title: Bookworms Are Real Insects xFunFacts
facts.summary: [xFunFacts] Bookworms aren't just a figure of speech. Tiny insects really can damage books, especially when they're stored in damp conditions.

facts.title: Bottlenose Whales Can Dive 915 Meters in Two Minutes xFunFacts
facts.summary: [xFunFacts] Northern bottlenose whales can dive about 915 meters in only two minutes, showcasing remarkable deep-sea adaptations.
facts.alt: Northern bottlenose whale diving deep underwater

facts.title: Bringing Bears to the Beach Is Illegal in Israel xFunFacts
facts.summary: [xFunFacts] Israel has some unusual laws, but one of the strangest is a rule that makes bringing a bear to the beach illegal.

facts.title: Octopuses Have Blue Blood and a Distributed Nervous System xFunFacts

facts.title: One Honeybee Can Visit 5,000 Flowers a Day xFunFacts
facts.summary: [xFunFacts] A single honeybee may visit up to 5,000 flowers in one day while collecting nectar and pollen.

facts.title: One Llama Can Protect an Entire Sheep Herd xFunFacts
facts.summary: [xFunFacts] Farmers have discovered an unlikely bodyguard for sheep. Just one fearless llama can keep an entire flock safe from coyotes.

facts.title: One-Third of Cats Feel Nothing From Catnip xFunFacts

facts.title: Only a Small Number of Shark Species Are Dangerous to Humans xFunFacts

facts.title: Only Female Mosquitoes Bite xFunFacts
facts.summary: [xFunFacts] Only female mosquitoes bite because they need nutrients from blood to produce eggs, while males feed on nectar.

facts.title: Only Four Bee Species Produce Honey xFunFacts
facts.summary: [xFunFacts] Only a few bee species produce enough honey for commercial harvesting, even though thousands of bee species exist worldwide.

facts.title: Only Pregnant Polar Bears Hibernate xFunFacts

facts.title: Only Three Bat Species Drink Blood xFunFacts

facts.title: Only Two Mammals Naturally Enjoy Spicy Food xFunFacts
facts.summary: [xFunFacts] Humans and tree shrews are the only known mammals that naturally enjoy spicy foods because of differences in capsaicin sensitivity.

facts.title: Opossums Don't Really Play Dead on Purpose xFunFacts
facts.summary: [xFunFacts] Opossums do not consciously play dead but enter an involuntary defensive state when terrified by predators.

facts.title: Over 80% of Australia's Animals and Plants Are Unique xFunFacts

facts.title: Owls Can Rotate Their Heads 270 Degrees xFunFacts
facts.summary: [xFunFacts] Owls can rotate their heads up to 270 degrees thanks to specialized neck anatomy that expands their field of vision.

facts.title: Owls Can't Move Their Eyes in Their Sockets xFunFacts
facts.summary: [xFunFacts] Owls cannot move their eyes inside their sockets, so they rotate their heads to scan their surroundings with remarkable precision.

facts.title: Owls Fly Almost Silently xFunFacts
facts.summary: [xFunFacts] Silent flight gives owls a hunting advantage. See how specialized feathers allow them to fly with almost no sound.

facts.title: Owls Have Asymmetrical Ears xFunFacts
facts.summary: [xFunFacts] Asymmetrical ears help owls locate prey with remarkable accuracy, even when hidden beneath snow or leaves.

facts.title: Owls Live on Every Continent Except Antarctica xFunFacts
facts.summary: [xFunFacts] Owls live on every continent except Antarctica, thriving in forests, deserts, mountains, wetlands, and cities.

facts.title: Owning an Eagle Feather Can Be Illegal in the U.S. xFunFacts

facts.alt: Protected eagle feather under U.S. federal law

facts.title: Owning Just One Guinea Pig Is Illegal in Switzerland xFunFacts
facts.summary: [xFunFacts] In Switzerland, owning a single guinea pig is against the law because these social animals are considered unhappy living alone.
facts.alt: Two guinea pigs together in Switzerland

facts.title: Panda Populations Are Recovering xFunFacts
facts.summary: [xFunFacts] Panda populations are recovering thanks to habitat protection, conservation programs, and successful breeding efforts.

facts.title: Pandas Can Climb Trees and Swim xFunFacts
facts.summary: [xFunFacts] Giant pandas can both climb trees and swim, showing surprising agility despite their large size.

facts.title: Pandas Eat Almost Nothing but Bamboo xFunFacts
facts.summary: [xFunFacts] Giant pandas obtain about 99% of their diet from bamboo despite belonging to the order of carnivorous mammals.

facts.title: Pandas Have a Pseudo-Thumb xFunFacts
facts.summary: [xFunFacts] Pandas use a specialized pseudo-thumb to grip bamboo efficiently, making feeding easier despite their bear ancestry.

facts.title: Pandas Have Extremely Powerful Jaws xFunFacts
facts.summary: [xFunFacts] Giant pandas have powerful jaws and strong teeth that allow them to crush tough bamboo stems with ease every day.

facts.title: Pandas Help Spread Seeds Through Forests xFunFacts
facts.summary: [xFunFacts] Pandas help spread seeds through forests as plant material sticks to their fur and passes through their habitat.

facts.title: Pandas Prefer Living Alone xFunFacts
facts.summary: [xFunFacts] Giant pandas prefer living alone and communicate through scent marking rather than social groups.

facts.title: Pandas Spend Most of Their Day Eating xFunFacts
facts.summary: [xFunFacts] Giant pandas spend up to 12 hours each day eating bamboo to meet their surprisingly high energy needs.

facts.title: Pangolins Are the Only Mammals Covered in Scales xFunFacts
facts.summary: [xFunFacts] Pangolins are the world's only mammals covered entirely in protective keratin scales.

facts.title: Pelicans Can Eat One-Third of Their Body Weight in One Meal xFunFacts
facts.summary: [xFunFacts] Pelicans can consume up to one-third of their body weight in a single meal thanks to their expandable throat pouch.

facts.title: Penguins Are Fast and Agile Swimmers xFunFacts
facts.summary: [xFunFacts] Penguins are powerful swimmers that can reach speeds of up to 25 mph beneath the water.

facts.title: Penguins Are Flightless Birds xFunFacts
facts.summary: [xFunFacts] Penguins are flightless birds that thrive in the Southern Hemisphere by using their wings as powerful swimming flippers.

facts.title: Penguins Can Jump Up to Six Feet High xFunFacts
facts.summary: [xFunFacts] Penguins can leap as high as six feet out of the water using powerful flipper strokes and impressive swimming speed.

facts.title: Penguins Can Safely Drink Seawater xFunFacts
facts.summary: [xFunFacts] Penguins can safely drink seawater because specialized glands remove excess salt from their bodies.

facts.title: Penguins Communicate with Calls and Body Language xFunFacts
facts.summary: [xFunFacts] Penguins communicate through unique calls and body movements to recognize mates, chicks, and defend territory.

facts.title: Penguins Have Existed for Over 60 Million Years xFunFacts
facts.summary: [xFunFacts] Penguins have lived on Earth for more than 60 million years, surviving dramatic changes throughout their evolution.

facts.title: Penguins Live Naturally Only in the Southern Hemisphere xFunFacts
facts.summary: [xFunFacts] Wild penguins live naturally only in the Southern Hemisphere, from Antarctica to South America, Africa, Australia, and beyond.

facts.title: Penguins Spend Half Their Lives in Water xFunFacts
facts.summary: [xFunFacts] Penguins divide their lives between land and water, breeding on shore and hunting in the ocean.

facts.title: Penguins Stay Warm with Blubber and Dense Feathers xFunFacts
facts.summary: [xFunFacts] Thick blubber and waterproof feathers help penguins stay warm in some of the coldest places on Earth.

facts.title: Pet Hamsters Can Run Several Miles in One Night xFunFacts
facts.summary: [xFunFacts] Pet hamsters may run several miles each night, reflecting the natural instincts of their wild ancestors.

facts.title: Pig Beach Is an Island Full of Swimming Pigs xFunFacts
facts.summary: [xFunFacts] Imagine an island where pigs swim in crystal-clear water. Pig Beach in the Bahamas is real and has become a world-famous attraction.

facts.title: Pigeons Can Tell Monet From Picasso xFunFacts
facts.summary: [xFunFacts] Research shows pigeons can distinguish paintings by artists such as Monet and Picasso.

facts.summary: [xFunFacts] A pig's neck structure limits how far it can tilt its head, making it difficult to look straight upward.

facts.title: Pigs Rank Among the Smartest Animals xFunFacts
facts.summary: [xFunFacts] Pigs are considered among the smartest animals thanks to their memory and problem-solving skills. Studies continue to reveal their impressive intelligence.

facts.title: Pit Bulls Rank Among the Most Affectionate Dogs xFunFacts
facts.summary: [xFunFacts] Pit Bulls often score highly in tests measuring affection toward humans. Their behavior depends heavily on training, socialization, and environment.

facts.title: Pizzly Bear: The Polar–Grizzly Hybrid xFunFacts

facts.title: Platypuses Glow Under Ultraviolet Light xFunFacts
facts.summary: [xFunFacts] Platypuses glow bluish-green under ultraviolet light, adding another mystery to this remarkable mammal.

facts.title: Polar Bears Are Powerful Long-Distance Swimmers xFunFacts
facts.summary: [xFunFacts] Polar bears are powerful swimmers capable of traveling for hours across icy Arctic waters in search of food and sea ice.

facts.title: Polar Bears Are the Largest Land Carnivores xFunFacts
facts.summary: [xFunFacts] Polar bears are the world's largest land carnivores, perfectly adapted for hunting in the Arctic environment.

facts.title: Polar Bears Can Eat 100 Pounds in One Meal xFunFacts
facts.summary: [xFunFacts] A hungry polar bear can eat about 100 pounds of food in a single meal. This massive appetite helps the animal survive long periods without hunting success.

facts.title: Polar Bears Can Sprint Up to 25 mph xFunFacts
facts.summary: [xFunFacts] Polar bears can sprint up to 25 mph over short distances despite being the largest bears on Earth.

facts.title: Polar Bears Have an Extraordinary Sense of Smell xFunFacts
facts.summary: [xFunFacts] A polar bear's extraordinary sense of smell can detect seals from as far as five miles away under favorable conditions.

facts.title: Polar Bears Have Black Skin Beneath White Fur xFunFacts
facts.summary: [xFunFacts] Polar bears have black skin beneath their white fur, helping them absorb warmth from the Arctic sun.

facts.title: Polar Bears Have Massive Paws xFunFacts
facts.summary: [xFunFacts] Polar bears have enormous paws that help them walk on ice, swim efficiently, and distribute their weight across snow.

facts.title: Polar Bears Hunt Walruses by Causing Stampedes xFunFacts
facts.summary: [xFunFacts] Polar bears sometimes hunt enormous walruses by creating chaos, triggering deadly stampedes instead of attacking directly.

facts.title: Police Dogs Often Learn Foreign-Language Commands xFunFacts
facts.summary: [xFunFacts] Police dogs often learn commands in languages such as German or Dutch to improve consistency during training and work.

facts.title: Poodles Are Among the Cleanest Dog Breeds xFunFacts
facts.summary: [xFunFacts] Poodles are considered one of the cleanest dog breeds because they shed very little and rarely develop strong odors. Their coat also makes them popular with many allergy-sensitive owners.

facts.title: Porcupines Float in Water xFunFacts
facts.summary: [xFunFacts] Porcupines float easily because air trapped inside their quills increases their natural buoyancy.

facts.title: Praying Mantises Can Turn Their Heads and See in 3D xFunFacts
facts.summary: [xFunFacts] Praying mantises can turn their heads and use binocular vision to judge distance with remarkable accuracy.

facts.title: Queen Alexandra's Birdwing Is the Largest Butterfly xFunFacts
facts.summary: [xFunFacts] Queen Alexandra's birdwing is the world's largest butterfly, with an impressive wingspan reaching up to 11 inches.

facts.title: Queen Termites Can Live Up to 50 Years xFunFacts
facts.summary: [xFunFacts] Queen termites can live up to 50 years, making them among the longest-lived insects known to science.

facts.title: Rabbits Can See Behind Themselves Without Turning Their Heads xFunFacts

facts.title: Rats Can Laugh When Tickled xFunFacts

facts.title: Rats Can Multiply Extremely Quickly xFunFacts

facts.title: Red Pandas Have No Close Living Relatives xFunFacts

facts.title: Reindeer Are Native to the Arctic xFunFacts

facts.title: Reindeer Can See Ultraviolet Light xFunFacts

facts.title: Reindeer Enjoy Eating Bananas xFunFacts
facts.summary: [xFunFacts] Reindeer happily eat bananas as occasional treats in zoos and wildlife parks, although they are not part of their natural diet.

facts.title: Reindeer Hair Is Hollow xFunFacts

facts.title: Reindeer Noses Warm the Air xFunFacts
facts.summary: [xFunFacts] Reindeer warm freezing air inside their noses before it reaches their lungs, helping them survive harsh Arctic winters.

facts.title: Rhinoceroses Have Three Toes on Each Foot xFunFacts
facts.summary: [xFunFacts] Rhinoceroses have three toes on each foot, giving these massive animals the stability needed to support their enormous weight.

facts.title: Roosters Can't Crow Without Stretching Their Necks xFunFacts

facts.title: Scientists Have Identified at Least 1,500 Bat Species xFunFacts

facts.summary: [xFunFacts] Scorpions glow under ultraviolet light because compounds in their outer shell naturally fluoresce.

facts.summary: [xFunFacts] Many seahorse pairs form long-term bonds, and males carry the developing young in a specialized brood pouch.

facts.title: Sharks Can Sense Blood from 4 Kilometers Away xFunFacts
facts.summary: [xFunFacts] Sharks have an exceptional sense of smell and can detect tiny traces of substances in water over impressive distances.

facts.summary: [xFunFacts] Sharks have lived in Earth's oceans for over 400 million years, predating both dinosaurs and flowering plants.

facts.title: Siberian Tigers Are the Largest Tigers xFunFacts
facts.summary: [xFunFacts] Siberian tigers are the largest tiger subspecies, built to survive harsh winters in northeastern Asia.

facts.title: Sloths Can Hold Their Breath for 40 Minutes xFunFacts

facts.title: Small Dogs Generally Live Longer Than Large Dogs xFunFacts
facts.summary: [xFunFacts] Smaller dog breeds generally live longer than larger breeds, although genetics and overall care also affect lifespan.

facts.summary: [xFunFacts] Long before humans notice an earthquake, snakes may already be sensing subtle changes beneath the ground.

facts.summary: [xFunFacts] Some frogs survive freezing winters by thawing back to life when temperatures rise in spring.

facts.title: Some Owls Can Look Almost Upside Down xFunFacts

facts.summary: [xFunFacts] Some penguin species can hold their breath underwater for up to 20 minutes while searching for food.

facts.summary: [xFunFacts] Some shrimp begin life as males and later become females, demonstrating one of nature's remarkable reproductive strategies.

facts.title: Some Tarantulas Can Survive Years Without Food xFunFacts
facts.summary: [xFunFacts] Some tarantulas can survive for years without food by relying on their slow metabolism and stored energy.

facts.title: Spider Silk Is Stronger Than Steel xFunFacts
facts.summary: [xFunFacts] Spider silk is stronger than steel of the same thickness while remaining lightweight, flexible, and incredibly durable.

facts.summary: [xFunFacts] Spiders live on every continent except Antarctica, thriving in forests, deserts, caves, wetlands, and even homes.

facts.title: Spiny Dogfish Sharks Can Live for Around 100 Years xFunFacts
facts.summary: [xFunFacts] Spiny dogfish sharks can live for around 100 years, making them among the longest-lived shark species ever studied.

facts.title: Squirrels Climb Trees Faster Than They Run xFunFacts

facts.title: Starfish Can Turn Their Stomachs Inside Out xFunFacts

facts.title: Swans Have Over 25,000 Feathers xFunFacts

facts.title: Swordfish Can Reach 108 km/h xFunFacts

facts.title: Tasmania Has Only Three Snake Species xFunFacts

facts.title: The Australian Dragonfly Is One of the Fastest Insects xFunFacts

facts.title: The Average Squirrel Lives About Nine Years xFunFacts

facts.title: The Bee Hummingbird Is the World's Smallest Bird xFunFacts

facts.title: The Black-Footed Cat Is the World's Smallest Wild Cat xFunFacts

facts.title: The Bumblebee Bat Is the Smallest Bat xFunFacts

facts.title: The Elf Owl Is the Smallest Owl xFunFacts

facts.title: The French Bulldog Is One of America's Most Popular Dogs xFunFacts
facts.summary: [xFunFacts] French Bulldogs have become one of America's favorite dog breeds because of their friendly personality and compact size.

facts.title: The Galápagos Penguin Lives North of the Equator xFunFacts

facts.title: The Giant Anteater’s Scientific Name Describes Its Body xFunFacts

facts.title: The Giant Panda Is China's National Treasure xFunFacts

facts.title: The Goliath Birdeater Is the Largest Spider xFunFacts

facts.title: The Hobo Spider Is a Real Spider Species xFunFacts

facts.title: The Kakapo Is the Only Flightless Parrot xFunFacts

facts.title: The King Cobra Is the World's Longest Venomous Snake xFunFacts

facts.title: The Lion's Mane Jellyfish Has Enormous Tentacles xFunFacts

facts.title: Liquid Water Can't Last Long on Mars xFunFacts
facts.summary: [xFunFacts] Liquid water cannot remain on Mars for long because the planet's thin atmosphere causes it to freeze or evaporate quickly.

facts.title: Looking at the Stars Is Looking into the Past xFunFacts
facts.summary: [xFunFacts] Looking at distant stars means seeing light that began its journey years, centuries, or even thousands of years ago.

facts.title: M&M's Were the First Candy Eaten in Space xFunFacts
facts.summary: [xFunFacts] M&M's became the first candy eaten in space thanks to their hard shell, which made them ideal for astronauts in zero gravity.

facts.title: Many Different Animals Have Traveled to Space xFunFacts
facts.summary: [xFunFacts] Animals including dogs, chimpanzees, monkeys, and mice traveled to space, helping scientists understand how living organisms adapt to spaceflight.

facts.title: Mariner 10 Mapped Nearly Half of Mercury xFunFacts
facts.summary: [xFunFacts] Mariner 10 became the first spacecraft to visit Mercury. Its flybys revealed nearly half of the planet's heavily cratered surface.

facts.title: Mars Has a Thin Carbon Dioxide Atmosphere xFunFacts
facts.summary: [xFunFacts] Mars has a thin atmosphere made mostly of carbon dioxide, providing little protection from harmful radiation.

facts.title: Mars Has an Average Temperature of About -62°C xFunFacts
facts.summary: [xFunFacts] Mars has an average surface temperature of about -62°C, making it far colder than even Earth's coldest inhabited regions.

facts.title: Mars Has Giant Dust Devils xFunFacts
facts.summary: [xFunFacts] Dust devils on Mars can grow hundreds of meters wide and several kilometers tall across the planet's dry surface.
facts.alt: Large dust devil crossing the Martian landscape

facts.title: Mars Has More Storms Near the Sun xFunFacts
facts.summary: [xFunFacts] Mars experiences more frequent and powerful dust storms when it moves closer to the Sun. Higher temperatures increase atmospheric activity across the planet.

facts.title: Mars Has Much Weaker Gravity Than Earth xFunFacts
facts.summary: [xFunFacts] Gravity on Mars is only about 38% as strong as Earth's, making objects and people weigh much less.

facts.title: Mars Has No Global Magnetic Field xFunFacts
facts.summary: [xFunFacts] Mars lacks a global magnetic field, leaving its surface exposed to intense solar and cosmic radiation.
facts.alt: Mars without a global magnetic field

facts.title: Mars Has Planet-Wide Dust Storms xFunFacts
facts.summary: [xFunFacts] Planet-wide dust storms can engulf Mars for weeks, dramatically changing visibility and surface conditions.

facts.title: Mars Has Polar Ice Caps Made of Water and Carbon Dioxide xFunFacts
facts.summary: [xFunFacts] Mars has polar ice caps made of frozen water and carbon dioxide that expand and shrink with the seasons.

facts.title: Mars Has Received More Space Missions Than Any Other Planet xFunFacts
facts.summary: [xFunFacts] Mars has hosted more robotic missions than any other planet as scientists search for evidence of ancient water and life.

facts.title: Mars Has Seasons Like Earth xFunFacts
facts.summary: [xFunFacts] Mars experiences spring, summer, autumn, and winter because its axis is tilted much like Earth's.

facts.title: Mars Has the Largest Canyon in the Solar System xFunFacts
facts.summary: [xFunFacts] Valles Marineris on Mars is the largest canyon in the solar system, stretching thousands of kilometers.

facts.title: Mars Has the Solar System's Largest Volcanoes and Canyons xFunFacts
facts.summary: [xFunFacts] Mars is home to Olympus Mons and Valles Marineris, two of the largest volcanic and canyon systems in the Solar System.
facts.alt: Olympus Mons and Valles Marineris on Mars

facts.title: Mars Has Two Small Moons xFunFacts
facts.summary: [xFunFacts] Mars has two small moons named Phobos and Deimos, both irregularly shaped satellites that orbit close to the planet.

facts.title: Mars Has Two Very Different Hemispheres xFunFacts
facts.summary: [xFunFacts] Mars has two contrasting hemispheres, with smooth northern plains and heavily cratered southern highlands.

facts.title: Mars Is Extremely Cold xFunFacts
facts.summary: [xFunFacts] Mars has an average temperature near -80°F, making it one of the coldest planets in the solar system.

facts.title: Mars Is Known as the Red Planet xFunFacts
facts.summary: [xFunFacts] Mars is called the Red Planet because iron oxide, commonly known as rust, covers much of its surface.

facts.title: Mars Is Not a Perfect Sphere xFunFacts
facts.summary: [xFunFacts] Mars is not perfectly round but slightly flattened, giving the Red Planet a shape closer to a rugby ball than a sphere.

facts.title: Mars Looks Red Because of Rusty Iron Minerals xFunFacts
facts.summary: [xFunFacts] Mars looks red because iron-rich minerals on its surface have rusted over billions of years through oxidation.

facts.title: Mars May Have Lost Its Thick Atmosphere After Giant Impacts xFunFacts
facts.summary: [xFunFacts] Giant impacts and solar wind likely stripped away much of Mars' once-thicker atmosphere, transforming the planet over time.
facts.alt: Mars with a thin atmosphere above its surface

facts.title: Mars May Once Have Had Flowing Water xFunFacts
facts.summary: [xFunFacts] Scientists have found strong evidence that rivers, lakes, and flowing water once existed on ancient Mars.

facts.title: Mars Was Named After the Roman God of War xFunFacts
facts.summary: [xFunFacts] Mars was named after the Roman god of war because its reddish appearance reminded ancient observers of blood and battle.
facts.alt: Planet Mars against a star-filled sky

facts.title: Mercury and Venus Are the Only Planets Without Moons xFunFacts
facts.summary: [xFunFacts] Every planet has at least one moon except two. Mercury and Venus stand alone for reasons that continue to interest astronomers.
facts.alt: Mercury and Venus shown without moons beside other planets with satellites.

facts.title: Mercury Has a Highly Elliptical Orbit xFunFacts
facts.summary: [xFunFacts] Mercury follows a highly elliptical orbit that greatly changes its distance from the Sun throughout the year.

facts.title: Mercury Has an Enormous Iron Core xFunFacts
facts.summary: [xFunFacts] Mercury's enormous iron core makes the small planet unusually dense compared with other rocky worlds.

facts.title: Mercury Has Extreme Temperatures xFunFacts
facts.summary: [xFunFacts] Mercury's daytime temperatures can reach 800°F before plunging to about -290°F after sunset.

facts.title: Mercury Has Ice at Its Poles xFunFacts
facts.summary: [xFunFacts] Water ice survives inside permanently shadowed craters near Mercury's poles despite the planet's intense heat.
facts.alt: Water ice inside Mercury's polar craters

facts.title: Mercury Has Virtually No Atmosphere xFunFacts
facts.summary: [xFunFacts] Mercury has virtually no true atmosphere, leaving it without weather, clouds, or wind. Only an extremely thin exosphere surrounds the planet.

facts.title: Mercury Is Earth's Closest Planet on Average xFunFacts
facts.summary: [xFunFacts] Over long periods, Mercury is Earth's closest neighboring planet because of the way planetary orbits overlap.
facts.alt: Mercury orbit compared with Earth and Venus

facts.title: Mercury, Venus, Earth, and Mars Are the Inner Planets xFunFacts
facts.summary: [xFunFacts] Mercury, Venus, Earth, and Mars make up the Solar System's four inner planets. These rocky worlds share important features but each evolved in a unique way.
facts.alt: Mercury, Venus, Earth, and Mars inner planets

facts.title: Mercury's Gravity Is Similar to Mars xFunFacts
facts.summary: [xFunFacts] Mercury's gravity is only about 38% as strong as Earth's, making objects weigh much less there.
facts.alt: Gravity comparison between Mercury and Earth

facts.title: Methane Gives Neptune Its Blue Color xFunFacts
facts.summary: [xFunFacts] Methane absorbs red light in Neptune's atmosphere, creating the planet's striking deep blue appearance seen from space.

facts.title: Moon Footprints Can Last Millions of Years xFunFacts
facts.summary: [xFunFacts] Footprints on the Moon can survive for millions of years. With no wind or rain, even Apollo astronaut tracks remain almost untouched.
facts.alt: Astronaut footprints preserved on the Moon's dusty surface.

facts.title: Moonlight Is Reflected Sunlight xFunFacts
facts.summary: [xFunFacts] Moonlight is simply sunlight reflected from the Moon's surface, creating the familiar glow seen in Earth's night sky.

facts.title: Moonlight Reaches Earth in Just 1.3 Seconds xFunFacts
facts.summary: [xFunFacts] Moonlight travels nearly 384,400 kilometers to Earth in just 1.3 seconds, revealing the astonishing speed of light through a simple example.

facts.title: More Than 40 Missions Have Been Sent to Mars xFunFacts
facts.summary: [xFunFacts] More than 40 space missions have explored Mars, revealing new clues about its geology, climate, and ancient history.

facts.title: More Than One Million Earths Could Fit Inside the Sun xFunFacts
facts.summary: [xFunFacts] The Sun is so massive that more than one million Earths could fit inside its volume.
facts.alt: Sun compared with one million Earths

facts.title: Most of Earth's Gold Is Hidden in the Core xFunFacts
facts.summary: [xFunFacts] Scientists estimate that about 99% of Earth's gold remains locked deep inside the planet's core.
facts.alt: Earth's core containing most of its gold

facts.title: Most People on Earth Can See the ISS xFunFacts
facts.summary: [xFunFacts] More than 90% of humanity lives where the International Space Station can occasionally be seen crossing the night sky.

facts.title: Most Stars Live for Billions of Years xFunFacts
facts.summary: [xFunFacts] Most stars spend billions of years producing energy, with their total lifespans determined mainly by their size and mass.
facts.alt: Stars at different stages of their life cycle

facts.title: NASA Once Pranked the World About Water on Mars xFunFacts
facts.summary: [xFunFacts] Even NASA has celebrated April Fool's Day, once convincing countless people that water had finally been discovered on Mars.

facts.title: NASA Plans to Return Humans to the Moon xFunFacts
facts.summary: [xFunFacts] NASA's Artemis program aims to return astronauts to the Moon and support long-term human exploration beyond Earth.
facts.alt: NASA Artemis mission to the Moon

facts.title: NASA's Curiosity Rover Takes Selfies on Mars xFunFacts
facts.summary: [xFunFacts] NASA's Curiosity rover creates detailed selfies by combining many images captured with its robotic arm-mounted camera.
facts.alt: NASA Curiosity rover on the Martian surface

facts.title: Neptune Completed Its First Known Orbit in 2011 xFunFacts
facts.summary: [xFunFacts] Neptune completed its first full orbit since its 1846 discovery in 2011 after traveling around the Sun for 165 years.

facts.title: Neptune Has 14 Known Moons xFunFacts
facts.summary: [xFunFacts] Neptune has 14 known moons, including Triton, one of the solar system's most fascinating and geologically active satellites.

facts.title: Neptune Has the Fastest Planetary Winds xFunFacts
facts.summary: [xFunFacts] Neptune's winds can roar past 1,200 miles per hour, faster than those on any other planet in our Solar System.

facts.title: Neptune Has Thin Rings of Ice and Dust xFunFacts
facts.summary: [xFunFacts] Neptune's faint rings are made of icy dust particles held in orbit by gravity and nearby moons.

facts.title: Neptune Is Extremely Cold xFunFacts
facts.summary: [xFunFacts] Neptune's upper atmosphere reaches about -373°F, making it one of the coldest planets in the solar system.

facts.title: Neptune Is Made Mostly of Hydrogen and Helium xFunFacts
facts.summary: [xFunFacts] Neptune's atmosphere is mostly hydrogen and helium, with methane adding its famous blue color and helping shape its unique weather.

facts.title: Neptune Was Discovered Through Mathematics xFunFacts
facts.summary: [xFunFacts] Neptune became the first planet located through mathematical predictions before astronomers confirmed it with a telescope.

facts.title: Neptune's Interior Is Rich in Ice and Rock xFunFacts
facts.summary: [xFunFacts] Neptune's interior contains rock along with water, ammonia, and methane in compressed icy layers beneath its atmosphere.

facts.title: Neptune's Moon Triton Is Falling Inward xFunFacts
facts.summary: [xFunFacts] Triton, Neptune's largest moon, is slowly spiraling toward the planet. Scientists believe it could eventually break apart into a ring system.

facts.title: Neptune's Rings Honor Famous Astronomers xFunFacts
facts.summary: [xFunFacts] Neptune's rings honor astronomers whose work helped predict, discover, and study the distant ice giant.

facts.title: North Korea Operates Its Own Space Program xFunFacts
facts.summary: [xFunFacts] North Korea has operated its own space program for decades despite limited success. Its launches continue attracting worldwide political and scientific attention.
facts.alt: North Korean satellite rocket launching from a coastal facility

facts.title: Olympus Mons Is Three Times Taller Than Everest xFunFacts
facts.summary: [xFunFacts] Olympus Mons on Mars is so enormous that Mount Everest would look tiny by comparison, standing only about one-third as tall.

facts.title: One Day on Mercury Lasts 58 Earth Days xFunFacts
facts.summary: [xFunFacts] Mercury rotates so slowly that one full day on its axis lasts about 58.6 Earth days. See why this planet has such an unusual rotation.

facts.title: One Day on Venus Lasts Almost an Earth Year xFunFacts
facts.summary: [xFunFacts] One day on Venus lasts nearly an Earth year because the planet rotates incredibly slowly.

facts.title: One Day on Venus Lasts Almost Eight Earth Months xFunFacts
facts.summary: [xFunFacts] A single day on Venus lasts almost eight Earth months because the planet rotates extremely slowly on its axis.
facts.alt: Planet Venus beside Earth for day length comparison

facts.title: One Year on Neptune Lasts 165 Earth Years xFunFacts
facts.summary: [xFunFacts] One year on Neptune lasts 165 Earth years. Since its discovery, the distant planet has completed only a single trip around the Sun.
facts.alt: Neptune completing one long orbit around the Sun.

facts.title: Only About 5% of the Universe Is Ordinary Matter xFunFacts
facts.summary: [xFunFacts] Everything visible in the universe accounts for only about 5% of its total content. Most of the cosmos remains hidden in forms scientists still cannot explain.
facts.alt: Ordinary matter, dark matter, and dark energy

facts.title: Only Two Spacecraft Have Visited Mercury xFunFacts
facts.summary: [xFunFacts] Mariner 10 and MESSENGER are the only spacecraft to closely explore Mercury and study its surface.

facts.title: Our Solar System Contains More Than Just Planets xFunFacts
facts.summary: [xFunFacts] The solar system includes the Sun, eight planets, moons, dwarf planets, asteroids, comets, and countless smaller objects.

facts.title: Our Solar System Has a Boundary xFunFacts
facts.summary: [xFunFacts] The heliopause marks the outer boundary of our Solar System, where the Sun's influence gives way to interstellar space.

facts.title: Outer Space Begins About 62 Miles Above Earth xFunFacts
facts.summary: [xFunFacts] Outer space is commonly considered to begin about 62 miles above Earth at the internationally recognized Kármán line.
facts.alt: Boundary between Earth and outer space

facts.title: Outer Space Is Incredibly Cold xFunFacts
facts.summary: [xFunFacts] Outer space averages about -455°F, placing it only a few degrees above absolute zero.

facts.title: Over 500 Meteorites Reach Earth Each Year xFunFacts
facts.summary: [xFunFacts] More than 500 meteorites reach Earth's surface every year, offering scientists valuable clues about the early solar system.

facts.title: Pluto and Charon Always Face Each Other xFunFacts
facts.summary: [xFunFacts] Pluto and Charon always show the same face to each other. Their perfectly synchronized orbit makes them one of the Solar System's most unique pairs.
facts.alt: Pluto and Charon always facing each other while orbiting together.

facts.title: Pluto Has Five Known Moons xFunFacts
facts.summary: [xFunFacts] Pluto has five known moons, including Charon, the largest companion in its remarkable dwarf planet system.
facts.alt: Pluto and its five known moons

facts.title: Pluto Is Smaller Than the United States xFunFacts
facts.summary: [xFunFacts] Pluto is smaller than the continental United States. Its surprisingly small size helped shape its classification as a dwarf planet.
facts.alt: Pluto compared with the United States

facts.title: Pluto Is Sometimes Closer to the Sun Than Neptune xFunFacts
facts.summary: [xFunFacts] Pluto occasionally sneaks closer to the Sun than Neptune, despite spending most of its long journey much farther away.
facts.alt: Pluto orbit crossing inside Neptune's orbit

facts.title: Pluto Lives in the Kuiper Belt xFunFacts
facts.summary: [xFunFacts] Pluto is one of the largest objects in the Kuiper Belt beyond Neptune. This icy region is home to countless frozen worlds.

facts.title: Pluto Was Reclassified as a Dwarf Planet xFunFacts
facts.summary: [xFunFacts] Pluto was reclassified as a dwarf planet in 2006 after astronomers introduced a new definition of a planet.

facts.title: Potatoes Were the First Food Grown in Space xFunFacts
facts.summary: [xFunFacts] Potatoes became the first food crop successfully grown in space during scientific farming experiments.

facts.title: Red Dwarf Stars Can Live for Trillions of Years xFunFacts
facts.summary: [xFunFacts] Red dwarf stars burn their fuel so slowly that some may shine for up to 10 trillion years. Their lifespans far exceed the current age of the universe.

facts.title: Russia Has More Surface Area Than Pluto xFunFacts
facts.summary: [xFunFacts] Russia's surface area is larger than Pluto's, offering a surprising comparison between the world's biggest country and a dwarf planet.

facts.title: Sally Ride Was the First American Woman in Space xFunFacts
facts.summary: [xFunFacts] Sally Ride became the first American woman in space in 1983, inspiring generations to pursue science and space exploration.
facts.alt: Astronaut Sally Ride in NASA spacesuit

facts.title: Saturn Could Fit 755 Earths Inside It xFunFacts
facts.summary: [xFunFacts] Saturn is so massive that about 755 Earths could fit inside its volume. It is the second-largest planet in the Solar System.

facts.title: Saturn Could Float in Water xFunFacts
facts.summary: [xFunFacts] Saturn's low average density means it could theoretically float in water if an ocean large enough existed.

facts.title: Saturn Has a Giant Hexagon at Its North Pole xFunFacts
facts.summary: [xFunFacts] Saturn's north pole is home to a giant hexagon-shaped storm that has fascinated scientists for decades.

facts.title: Saturn Is Incredibly Cold xFunFacts
facts.summary: [xFunFacts] Saturn's upper atmosphere can reach temperatures as low as -288°F, making it one of the coldest worlds in the solar system.

facts.title: Saturn Is Nine Times Wider Than Earth xFunFacts
facts.summary: [xFunFacts] Saturn is about nine times wider than Earth, making it the second-largest planet in the solar system.
facts.alt: Saturn compared with Earth in size

facts.title: Saturn Is the Lightest Planet xFunFacts
facts.summary: [xFunFacts] Saturn is the second-largest planet but has the lowest average density in the solar system. It is so light that it would theoretically float in water.

facts.title: Saturn Is the Solar System's Second-Largest Planet xFunFacts
facts.summary: [xFunFacts] Saturn is the Solar System's second-largest planet, yet it is less dense than water. In theory, it could float in a gigantic ocean.
facts.alt: Saturn with its rings compared in size to Earth.

facts.title: Saturn's Moons May Support Life xFunFacts
facts.summary: [xFunFacts] Saturn's moons Enceladus and Titan are leading candidates in the search for environments that could support life.

facts.title: Saturn's Radio Signals Can't Reach Earth xFunFacts
facts.summary: [xFunFacts] Saturn produces natural radio emissions, but they are too weak to be detected directly from Earth.

facts.title: Saturn's Rings Are Mostly Ice and Rock xFunFacts
facts.summary: [xFunFacts] Saturn's magnificent rings are composed mainly of countless pieces of ice mixed with rocky material and dust.

facts.title: Saturn's Rings Are Surprisingly Thin xFunFacts
facts.summary: [xFunFacts] Saturn's rings are incredibly wide yet astonishingly thin. Their delicate structure is made mostly of countless pieces of water ice.

facts.title: Saturn's Rings Have Seven Main Groups xFunFacts
facts.summary: [xFunFacts] Saturn's famous rings are divided into seven main groups, each with unique structures and countless icy particles.

facts.title: Saturn's Rings May Be Ancient Debris xFunFacts
facts.summary: [xFunFacts] Saturn's rings may have formed from shattered moons, comets, or asteroids broken apart by the planet's gravity.

facts.title: Scientists Believe It May Rain Diamonds on Neptune and Uranus xFunFacts
facts.summary: [xFunFacts] Scientists believe extreme conditions inside Neptune and Uranus may create diamond rain deep beneath their clouds.
facts.alt: Diamond rain inside Neptune and Uranus

facts.title: Scientists Still Don't Know the Age of Saturn's Rings xFunFacts
facts.summary: [xFunFacts] Scientists continue studying Saturn's rings as they investigate when the planet's spectacular icy rings first formed.

facts.title: Scotland Created an Official Tartan for Mars Missions xFunFacts
facts.summary: [xFunFacts] Scotland even created an official tartan for future Mars missions, blending centuries-old tradition with space exploration.
facts.alt: Scottish tartan pattern for Mars missions

facts.title: Solar Flares Can Be Incredibly Powerful xFunFacts
facts.summary: [xFunFacts] Powerful solar flares can release energy equal to millions of atomic bombs in just minutes.
facts.alt: Powerful solar flare erupting from the Sun

facts.title: Solar Wind Creates the Northern and Southern Lights xFunFacts
facts.summary: [xFunFacts] Solar wind interacts with Earth's magnetic field to create the colorful Northern and Southern Lights near the poles.
facts.alt: Aurora created by the solar wind

facts.title: Some Radio Signals Began Before Earth Existed xFunFacts
facts.summary: [xFunFacts] Some radio signals arriving today began traveling long before Earth even existed. Astronomers use them to study the distant universe.
facts.alt: Ancient radio signals from deep space

facts.title: Sound Cannot Travel Through Space xFunFacts
facts.summary: [xFunFacts] Sound cannot travel through space because the vacuum contains almost no particles to carry vibrations.
facts.alt: Sound waves blocked in space vacuum

facts.title: Space Contains Chemicals That Smell Like Rum xFunFacts
facts.summary: [xFunFacts] A giant cloud in space contains molecules linked to the smell of rum and the flavor of raspberries. Cosmic chemistry can be surprisingly familiar.

facts.title: Space Isn't Completely Silent xFunFacts
facts.summary: [xFunFacts] Space cannot carry sound through a vacuum, yet scientists detect radio waves and cosmic vibrations with specialized instruments.

facts.title: Space Officially Begins at the Kármán Line xFunFacts
facts.summary: [xFunFacts] The Kármán Line is widely accepted as the point where outer space begins. It marks the transition from atmospheric flight to orbital travel.

facts.title: Space Smells Like Seared Steak xFunFacts
facts.summary: [xFunFacts] Astronauts often describe the scent left on spacesuits after spacewalks as similar to seared steak, hot metal, or welding fumes.

facts.title: Spacesuits Have a Built-In Scratch Pad xFunFacts
facts.summary: [xFunFacts] Spacesuits include a hidden Velcro patch that helps astronauts scratch an itchy nose. It's one of the simplest yet smartest features inside a helmet.

facts.title: Sputnik Was the First Artificial Satellite xFunFacts
facts.summary: [xFunFacts] Sputnik 1 became the world's first artificial satellite in 1957. Its successful launch marked the beginning of the modern Space Age.

facts.title: Stars Come in Different Colors xFunFacts
facts.summary: [xFunFacts] Stars appear red, yellow, white, or blue, with their color mainly determined by surface temperature.
facts.alt: Red, yellow, white, and blue stars in space

facts.title: Stars Twinkle Because of Earth's Atmosphere xFunFacts
facts.summary: [xFunFacts] Stars seem to sparkle because their light passes through Earth's atmosphere. The effect disappears when viewed from space.

facts.title: Sunlight Takes About 8 Minutes to Reach Earth xFunFacts
facts.summary: [xFunFacts] Every ray of sunlight you see left the Sun more than eight minutes ago. That travel time reveals the enormous distance between Earth and its star.
facts.alt: Sunlight traveling from Sun to Earth

facts.title: Sunlight Takes Over Four Hours to Reach Neptune xFunFacts
facts.summary: [xFunFacts] Sunlight takes more than four hours to travel from the Sun to distant Neptune across the outer solar system.

facts.title: Sunsets on Mars Appear Blue xFunFacts
facts.summary: [xFunFacts] Sunsets on Mars appear blue because fine atmospheric dust scatters light differently than Earth's atmosphere.
facts.alt: Blue sunset over the horizon on Mars

facts.title: Surface Tension Creates Floating Water Spheres in Space xFunFacts
facts.summary: [xFunFacts] Water naturally forms perfect floating spheres in space. Surface tension becomes the dominant force in the weightless environment aboard the ISS.
facts.alt: Floating spherical water droplets inside the International Space Station.

facts.title: The Asteroid Belt Lies Between Mars and Jupiter xFunFacts
facts.summary: [xFunFacts] The asteroid belt between Mars and Jupiter contains millions of rocky objects left over from the solar system's formation.
facts.alt: Asteroid belt between Mars and Jupiter

facts.title: The Core of a Comet Is Called a Nucleus xFunFacts
facts.summary: [xFunFacts] The solid center of a comet is called its nucleus. It consists of rock, dust, and frozen gases that release material as the comet approaches the Sun.

facts.title: The First Black Hole Photo Was Released in 2019 xFunFacts
facts.summary: [xFunFacts] Humanity captured its first image of a black hole in 2019. The achievement required radio telescopes spread across the entire Earth.

facts.title: The First Extragalactic Supernova Was Seen in 1885 xFunFacts
facts.summary: [xFunFacts] The first supernova ever observed beyond the Milky Way was recorded in 1885. It became an important milestone in astronomical history.

facts.title: The Four Inner Planets Are Rocky Worlds xFunFacts
facts.summary: [xFunFacts] Mercury, Venus, Earth, and Mars are the solar system's four rocky inner planets with solid surfaces and unique landscapes.

facts.title: The Great Wall of China Isn't Visible from Space xFunFacts
facts.summary: [xFunFacts] The Great Wall of China is not normally visible from space with the naked eye. The famous belief comes from a long-standing myth rather than astronaut observations.
facts.alt: Great Wall of China from orbit

facts.title: The Heliosphere Protects the Solar System xFunFacts
facts.summary: [xFunFacts] The heliosphere is a vast bubble created by the solar wind that helps shield the solar system from cosmic radiation.

facts.title: The International Space Station Has a Hidden Geocache xFunFacts
facts.summary: [xFunFacts] Even the International Space Station has a hidden geocache, giving astronauts a chance to join one of Earth's biggest treasure hunts.

facts.title: The International Space Station Is a Floating Space Laboratory xFunFacts
facts.summary: [xFunFacts] The International Space Station serves as an orbiting laboratory where astronauts conduct research in microgravity.

facts.title: The ISS Is the Largest Structure Ever Built in Space xFunFacts
facts.summary: [xFunFacts] The International Space Station is the largest structure humans have ever built in space. It circles Earth every 90 minutes at incredible speed.
facts.alt: International Space Station orbiting above Earth.

facts.title: The ISS Travels Faster Than 27,000 km/h xFunFacts
facts.summary: [xFunFacts] The International Space Station races around Earth at more than 27,000 km/h. Its speed allows astronauts to circle the planet every 90 minutes.

facts.title: The Kuiper Belt Lies Beyond Neptune xFunFacts
facts.summary: [xFunFacts] The Kuiper Belt beyond Neptune contains Pluto, dwarf planets, and countless icy objects left over from the solar system's formation.
facts.alt: Kuiper Belt beyond Neptune with Pluto

facts.title: The Longest Total Solar Eclipse Lasts About 7 Minutes 31 Seconds xFunFacts
facts.summary: [xFunFacts] The longest possible total solar eclipse lasts about 7 minutes 31 seconds under exceptionally favorable orbital conditions.
facts.alt: Total solar eclipse with the Sun's corona visible

facts.title: The Milky Way Contains Hundreds of Billions of Stars xFunFacts
facts.summary: [xFunFacts] Our Milky Way contains hundreds of billions of stars. Some giant galaxies hold hundreds of times more.

facts.title: The Milky Way Contains Over 200 Billion Stars xFunFacts
facts.summary: [xFunFacts] The Milky Way contains more than 200 billion stars, along with countless planets, gas clouds, and dark matter.

facts.title: The Moon Formed About 4.5 Billion Years Ago xFunFacts
facts.summary: [xFunFacts] Scientists believe the Moon formed about 4.5 billion years ago after a giant collision with the young Earth.
facts.alt: Formation of the Moon after a giant impact

facts.title: The Moon Had Volcanoes During the Dinosaur Age xFunFacts
facts.summary: [xFunFacts] The Moon was still volcanically active while dinosaurs roamed Earth, revealing a much longer geological history than many people realize.

facts.title: The Moon Has a Lemon-Like Shape xFunFacts
facts.summary: [xFunFacts] The Moon is not perfectly round but slightly elongated because of differences in its internal gravity.
facts.alt: Moon showing its slightly uneven shape

facts.title: The Moon Has a Small Iron Core xFunFacts
facts.summary: [xFunFacts] The Moon contains a small iron-rich core that offers clues about its internal structure and ancient evolution.
facts.alt: Cross-section of the Moon's iron core

facts.title: The Moon Has Extreme Temperature Swings xFunFacts
facts.summary: [xFunFacts] Without an atmosphere, the Moon experiences dramatic temperature swings between its long days and nights.

facts.title: The Moon Has Moonquakes xFunFacts
facts.summary: [xFunFacts] Moonquakes are lunar earthquakes that can last much longer than earthquakes on Earth because of the Moon's dry interior.

facts.title: The Moon Has Mountains, Valleys, and Plains xFunFacts
facts.summary: [xFunFacts] The Moon features mountains, valleys, craters, and volcanic plains that reveal its long geological history.
facts.alt: Mountains, valleys, and plains on the Moon

facts.title: The Moon Has No Atmosphere xFunFacts
facts.summary: [xFunFacts] The Moon has virtually no atmosphere, leaving its surface exposed to radiation, meteor impacts, and extreme temperatures.

facts.title: The Moon Is About 238,855 Miles from Earth xFunFacts
facts.summary: [xFunFacts] The Moon orbits about 238,855 miles from Earth, making it our closest natural neighbor in space.

facts.title: The Moon Is About 3,475 Kilometers Across xFunFacts
